common_errors: Omitting the fixed support's couple moment MA and solving as if only Ax and Ay existed.
Giving a roller a horizontal reaction or a pin a couple it cannot provide.
Choosing a moment center that retains all three unknowns in the moment equation when a support point would eliminate two of them.
Sign errors on moment arms when writing ΣM (wrong clockwise/counterclockwise contribution).
Reporting a negative solved reaction as an arithmetic error instead of reversing the assumed sense.
Attempting to solve an indeterminate layout (more than three independent reaction unknowns) with only ΣFx, ΣFy, and ΣM.
Omitting units or direction/sense when reporting reactions.
Treating the problem as a pin-and-roller beam reaction template when the support set is different (e.g., fixed).
procedure.concept: Solving 2D support reactions composes two parent skills: support_reaction_modeling tells which reaction components a support can exert (the motions it prevents), and rigid_body_equilibrium_2d supplies ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, and ΣM = 0 to find their values. Together they yield named reactions with magnitude, direction, and units. Moment-centre choice matters here because a well-chosen centre can eliminate two reaction components at once and leave a one-unknown moment equation — that is how determinate three-unknown systems stay tractable. This skill is the general 2D method for any support layout that is statically determinate. It is not support-type mapping alone (no values), not equilibrium on a pre-given FBD with non-reaction unknowns, and not the beam-specific pin-and-roller application already signed as beam_reactions — that skill applies this method to a simply supported beam; here the method itself is taught on a body that uses a different determinate support set.

failure_signal_mappings.trigger_condition: Student resolves the inclined applied force onto the wrong axes, swaps sine and cosine for the stated angle, or assigns Fx/Fy to the wrong directions — changing the solved reactions.

Student writes ΣFx, ΣFy, or ΣM_O with an incorrect reaction sense, a wrong moment-arm sign under the stated convention, omits the couple-moment reaction MA from ΣM, or inserts a couple into a force equation.
Student reports incomplete reactions (missing sense or units), proceeds on an indeterminate unknown count, or frames the solve as a pin-and-roller beam template when the support set is different.

formula.notation: ΣFx = 0 ; ΣFy = 0 ; ΣM_O = 0. Fixed (built-in) support at A → Ax, Ay, and couple MA (three unknowns). Inclined force F at angle θ above +x: F_x = F cos θ, F_y = F sin θ. Determinacy: number of independent reaction unknowns must equal 3 in 2D.

algebraic sum of force components in the +y direction
algebraic sum of moments about point O under the stated sign convention
horizontal reaction force component at the fixed support at A
vertical reaction force component at the fixed support at A

magnitude of the inclined applied force at free end B
x-component of F after resolution onto the stated axes
y-component of F after resolution onto the stated axes
inclination of F above the +x axis (cos θ and sin θ as stated)
length of bar AB from the fixed support at A to free end B

The synthesis skill: composes support_reaction_modeling (a3e5cba6, which components exist) with rigid_body_equilibrium_2d (fa62fbe8, what their values are). Both parents stopped deliberately short of it. Duplicate hazard against the already-signed beam_reactions cleared at the review beat: that skill is a simply supported beam, pin plus roller, vertical point loads, no inclined-force resolution and no couple reaction; this is the general 2D method taught on a fixed cantilever with an inclined end load, matching the graph's general-to-specific direction (support_reactions_2d is beam_reactions' prerequisite). Worked example independently re-derived by Operator and cross-checked by the vector moment r x F: bar AB, L = 4.0 m, fixed at A, F = 100 N at B at 53.1 degrees (cos 0.60, sin 0.80) resolving to Fx = 60 N, Fy = 80 N; SumFx = 0 gives Ax = -60 N (60 N left); SumFy = 0 gives Ay = -80 N (80 N down); SumM_A = MA + 320 = 0 gives MA = -320 N-m (320 N-m clockwise). Fx acts along the bar's own line through A, so its moment arm is zero. The moment equation is required: MA appears in neither force equation. Determinacy verified: exactly 3 reaction unknowns against 3 equations, and properly constrained — a fixed support supplies two force components plus a couple, not three concurrent or parallel force lines of action. This deliberately REVERSES support_reaction_modeling's example, which was indeterminate by design because modeling does not require solvability. 3-signal mapping, content-earned: axis_confusion at step 5 (inclined-force resolution) — verified LIVE, a sine/cosine swap gives Fx = 80, Fy = 60 and changes all three reactions to 80 N left, 60 N down, 240 N-m clockwise; sign_or_placement_error at step 7 (writing the three scalar equations including the couple reaction); unclassified at step 10 (reporting). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. procedure: Identify the rigid body and every support that supplies reactions; classify each support by type (pin, roller, fixed/built-in, cable/link).

Map each support type to its allowed reaction components using the constraint → reaction rule (fixed → two force components plus a couple moment; pin → two force components; roller → one force perpendicular to the surface; cable/link → one force along the member).
Draw the free-body diagram with those reaction components at the supports, assume positive senses, and place all applied loads at their given locations.

Count the independent reaction unknowns. Exactly three unknowns against the three 2D equilibrium equations is the necessary condition to proceed; stop if the count exceeds three (statically indeterminate — not solvable by equilibrium alone). Treat the count as a screening check, not a full determinacy verdict: proper-versus-improper constraint (concurrent or parallel reaction arrangements) belongs to constraints_static_determinacy.
Resolve every inclined applied force into x and y components using the stated axes and angle.
Choose a moment center O that eliminates as many unknown reactions as possible and state why (for a fixed support, O at the wall often removes Ax and Ay from the moment equation).
Write ΣFx = 0, ΣFy = 0, and ΣM_O = 0, substituting resolved components and including the couple-moment reaction where present.
Solve for every unknown reaction component and couple.
Interpret each signed result: a negative value means the true sense is opposite the assumed positive direction.
Report every support reaction with magnitude, direction or rotational sense, and units.

worked_example.answer: Ax = 60 N to the left; Ay = 80 N downward; MA = 320 N·m clockwise
worked_example.prompt: A rigid horizontal bar AB of length L = 4.0 m is built into a vertical wall at A (fixed / built-in support). Free end B carries an applied force F = 100 N directed at 53.1° above the +x axis (use cos 53.1° = 0.60 and sin 53.1° = 0.80). There are no other loads. Use +x to the right, +y upward, and counterclockwise moments positive. Find the support reactions at A.
solution_steps: Body: bar AB. Support: fixed (built-in) wall at A only.
Fixed support at A → three reactions: Ax (horizontal), Ay (vertical), and couple MA. No other supports.
FBD: Ax and Ay at A (assume +x and +y), MA at A (assume +CCW), applied F at B at 53.1° above +x.

Count: 3 reaction unknowns (Ax, Ay, MA) against 3 equilibrium equations → necessary condition met; solvable. Properly constrained here because the fixed support supplies two force components plus a couple, not three concurrent or parallel force lines of action.
Choose O = A: Ax and Ay act at A (zero moment arm), so ΣM_A involves only MA and the moments of Fx and Fy at B. Fy has arm L = 4.0 m; Fx is horizontal through A (zero arm).
Solve: Ax = −60 N; Ay = −80 N; MA = −320 N·m.
Sign interpretation: Ax = 60 N to the left (−x); Ay = 80 N downward (−y); MA = 320 N·m clockwise (opposite +CCW).
Report: Ax = 60 N to the left; Ay = 80 N downward; MA = 320 N·m clockwise.
